title: The kingdom within (Imitation 2.1)
hook: turn inward; Christ visits the inward person
tomorrow: how can a heavy thing get lighter without losing weight?

segments.voice: Yesterday the Imitation pointed past its own pages, to the eternal Word. Yesterday's line: truth teaches.

Maps pin everything now: the coffee shop, a friend's house, the little blue dot that is you. In Luke's Gospel, some Pharisees ask Jesus when the kingdom of God will come, and he says nobody will be able to point and say, look here, or look there: "for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you." No pin, no blue dot. The second book of the Imitation opens on that line. And readers don't all hear it the same way.
screen: `EVERYTHING HAS A PIN.` → `NOT HERE, NOT THERE.` → `WITHIN YOU.`

segments.voice: The first voice is the Imitation's, and it hears within as inward. Turn to the Lord with your whole heart, it says, let go of the restless outside world, and your soul will find rest. Care less for outward things, give yourself to inward ones, and you'll see the kingdom come within you. Christ will come, it promises, if you prepare a fitting place for him inside; he often visits the inward person, with gentle talk and deep peace. A second voice reads the same Greek words, entos hymon, as among you: the kingdom was standing right in front of the people asking, in Jesus himself, and it shows up between people, at a table, in a crowd. Some readers hear both at once. Let each make its best case. Inward: with no room inside, you'll walk right past the kingdom when it stands among you. Among: if it stays only inside, it never reaches the neighbor at your door. The Imitation doesn't pretend the inside is tidy, either. It talks about preparing a room, the way you'd ready one for a guest you love, because people and things change and fail, it says, but Christ stays to the end.
screen: `FIRST VOICE: INWARD.` · `SECOND VOICE: AMONG YOU.` · `EACH VIEW'S BEST CASE.` · `A ROOM MADE READY.` · then, large: `THE KINGDOM IS WITHIN.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and let the noise outside stay outside. Turn your attention inward, the way you'd clear a room before a guest arrives, setting aside one worry at a time. If you pray, you can wait there for Christ.
The kingdom within. Jesus' words in Luke, which the Imitation reads as an invitation to ready a room inside.
Pocket this one: the kingdom is within, in a room you get ready for a guest. Talk soon.

howItsDone: Some Christians keep a few minutes of inward prayer each day; others put more weight on finding the kingdom among people, in worship and service.

fork.setup: your small group splits: half say the kingdom is within, half say among you. you're on team within. what's the other side's best case?
options: if it stays inside you, it never reaches the neighbor at your door.

fork.reveal: the among-you reading says the kingdom stood in front of them in Jesus, and shows up between people. the Greek allows both, and the Imitation's inward room is the other half.

notes: The Imitation is paraphrased throughout (quoted: null), including 'Christ often visits the inward person' and 'people and things change and fail, but Christ stays to the end'; confirm it is fair to 2.1.
